name: Solomon's Plea to Westfall
summary: In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon sends an urgent appeal to Westfall for help against Blackrock orcs and gnolls. He asks Gryan Stoutmantle to send the People's Militia while Stormwind's royal army fails to answer.

sections.title: A Desperate Call for Aid
sections.body: Blackrock orcs and hostile gnolls threaten Redridge, and Magistrate Solomon is isolated in Lakeshire. Stormwind's royal army has not arrived in force to defend the region's borders. With no time to wait for support from the capital, Solomon writes to seek help beyond the regular army. Word has reached him of a volunteer defense force forming in Elwynn to the west, so he appeals to the People's Militia.

sections.title: Reaching Across the Border
sections.body: Solomon addresses his message to Gryan Stoutmantle, a veteran warrior organizing Westfall's frontier defense. He hopes Stoutmantle can spare fighters for Lakeshire until Stormwind sends regular reserves. An adventurer carries the document. With Stormwind's outlying territories poorly coordinated, local magistrates must arrange mutual aid on their own.

faq.q: What is Solomon's Plea to Westfall?
faq.answer: Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire writes to Gryan Stoutmantle, asking the People's Militia in Westfall to send reinforcements for Redridge's defense.

faq.q: Why is Magistrate Solomon asking Westfall for help instead of Stormwind?
faq.answer: Stormwind's royal troops have not arrived in force as Lakeshire's danger grows. With no time to wait for the Crown, Solomon seeks help from a nearby fighting force.
Gryan Stoutmantle leads the People's Militia, a volunteer defense league of local farmers and settlers protecting Westfall from the Defias Brotherhood.

faq.q: What threats are pushing Solomon to send this letter?
faq.answer: Blackrock orcs are invading, and gnolls raid throughout the Redridge Mountains, straining Lakeshire's town guard.

angles.text: For the Alliance, Solomon's appeal shows how outlying towns turn to local volunteers when royal troops do not arrive.
As a human, you can see how strained rural settlements have become, with the missing king and political neglect leaving frontier lands vulnerable.
